full_judgment: 16. In Title Suit No. 5 of 984 then renumbered as Title Suit No. 81 of 1992 petitioner was plaintiff. Predecessor of first and second-opposite parties Hasen Ali had been defendant No. 4 and on his death his heirs sons, daughters and wives including first and second-opposite parties had been substituted and first and second opposite parties were substituted as defendant Nos. 4(cha) and 4(Jaha), From certified copy of service return which has been produced before this Court it stood exposed to view that summons upon substituted defendants including substituted defendant Nos. 4(cha) and 4(Jaha) (first and second opposite parties) had been duly served and there was a declaration made by serving officer as to the service of summons upon them. From certified copy of order dated 7-2-1996 it is brought to light that learned Assistant Judge made a note in the order sheet that summons upon substituted defendants had been duly served. Learned Judge further noted that registered notices were kept with the record. Service of summons upon substituted defendants including substituted defendant No. 4(cha) and 4(jaha) who are (first and second opposite parties) is an evidence as to the service of summons as contemplated in rule 19A of Order V of the Code. The noting as to the due service of summons upon substituted defendants including defendant Nos. 4 (cha) and 9(jaha) (first and second opposite parties) dated 7-2-1996, also, got a strong presumption as mandated in section 114(e) of The Evidence Act of 1872.
